Voatdev

Last week in /v/voatdev started with a report about being able to post 7 posts within one day with a month-old account with 20 CCP, which allegedly should be limited to 5. I say "allegedly" because I am not aware of account age or CCP affecting the number of daily posts allowed, although such a rule would not surprise me. As far as I know, as long as a user has 10 CCP and they do not violate spam protection rules (multiple posts to one subverse within a small time frame, for example, will fulfil a post quota) they should be fine. At any rate, this user's submission page shows only 5 posts anyway, so either posts were deleted somehow without his noticing, he miscounted, or he is a troll.

There was another report about voting not being possible for a period of time, post saving being dysfunctional, and subscriptions not showing. It almost sounds like the user was not logged in! At any rate, all of these features are functional now, whether they were dysfunctional for a time or not -- and if they were I suspect it was an isolated case; browser or device related, perhaps.

Next was a question about Voat's servers being overworked by an influx of new users, and whether the userbase could do anything to dampen the effect.

There followed a suggestion to delete all posts after a certain period of time has elapsed since their posting. I am dubious about these kinds of suggestions; I think some of the value websites like Voat have is their ability to document events over time, and to be able to go back and find certain posts corresponding to certain events. Well organized subverses help with this, of course -- it's futile to try to find a specific post submitted to /v/whatever, for example. However, the suggestion to allow individual subverses to choose to delete all posts after a certain amount of time is, I think, a good idea.

Next was a troll post, where a user with an 'L' in his username created an alternate account with a capital 'i' in place of the lowercase 'L'. I don't think it's possible to do this anymore; there is account imitation code in place to prevent this. However, this alternate account was created 1.3 years ago, which probably precedes the code change.

There was then a report about the stunted URL parsing (there sure are a lot of these; I didn't realize ~ characters were so common in URLs...

There was also a request to stop recycling old ads due to them being "annoying". An interesting perspective I haven't heard before. In all honesty, the $50, or whatever it was, that those users spent to pay for those ads have to be among the best investments ever made on the internet.

Finally there was a question about why subverses with minimum CCP to downvote restrictions still get featured in the "Most viewed in the last 24 hours" window. I think this being the case is reasonable; not wanting subverses that disallow free downvoting to appear in /v/all can be justified in a number of ways, including not wanting subverses with "less genuine" votes to be represented on the front page, whereas the "Most viewed" window is supposed to be about pure insight into what threads on the website have been viewed the most -- whether the comments within such threads receive balanced votes or not is irrelevant to that.

VoatStatistics

Posts per day for last week: Thursday won the competition for most posts last week (as it is wont to do), but notably this week it was by several hundred posts. This is a result of the large influx of users last week. How large of an influx? Well, last week the total posts across Voat numbered 13,193 -- a 3,740 post increase from the week before. Notable!

Most commented posts for last week: The thread with the most comments and the most commenters last week was the landing thread for the influx of users, unsurprisingly. Certainly the most comments in one thread that I've reported on since starting this series of news reports. Interestingly, the comment and commenter numbers for this landing thread more than doubled the comments and number of commenters in Putt's stickied announcement in both fields.

Most controversial posts for last week: Interestingly, a joke was the most controversial post last week -- but not for its contents. Apparently the poster was encouraging upvote farming for the influx users, and referenced his joke post in a separate post calling for this farming. As is the usual, Voat users banded together to prevent other users from attempting to game the system.

Voat Updates

Last week, as previously mentioned, a large influx of users came to Voat as a result of their community being banned on reddit, as is the standard course. This prompted not one, not two, but three globally stickied announcements from Putt -- one to essentially acknowledge the influx; another to announce that updates were planned and that some downtime could be expected over the weekend; and a third to take pity on the new users and try to explain why they lacked the ability to make use of so many of Voat's CCP-dependent essential features.

The first announcement also dropped Voat's active BTC wallet address (3NZvuAk3Csf1UP1KCmzN9dhiXTwvhTgr9k), which is new enough to have not been seen before, despite replacing former addresses. I personally would encourage anyone with the means (financially and in terms of cryptocurrency familiarity) to donate monthly to Voat. Now that I know the correct address I will continue to do so myself. It is an important thing for us to do to help keep this website alive; it is thanks to cryptocurrency and generous users (and the sweat and blood of Putt of course) that is Voat still here.

Voat Banlog

One user was banned last week.

No domains were banned last week.

That concludes this report. Stay vigilant, goats.
